questions.stem: The IUPAC name of CH$_3$CH$_2$CHO is
questions.explanation: The chain has three carbons, so the parent is propane. The terminal -CHO group makes it an aldehyde, so the final -e of propane is replaced by -al, and the aldehyde carbon is numbered as C-1 automatically. The name is therefore propanal.

optionRationale.4: Ethanal has only two carbon atoms.

questions.stem: Formalin, used to preserve biological specimens, is
questions.explanation: Formalin is about 40 % methanal (formaldehyde) in water. It denatures proteins and acts as a preservative and disinfectant. It is not pure methanal, which is a gas at room temperature.

optionRationale.1: Ethanal is acetaldehyde, which is not the main component of formalin.
optionRationale.3: Methanal is a gas at room temperature, and formalin is its aqueous solution.
optionRationale.4: Methanol is the alcohol and not the aldehyde.

questions.objective: Recall the composition and use of formalin

questions.stem: Which of the following is the strongest acid?
questions.explanation: The electron withdrawing -NO$_2$ group disperses the negative charge of the carboxylate ion and stabilises it, so 4-nitrobenzoic acid is the strongest acid. Electron donating groups such as -CH$_3$ and -OCH$_3$ destabilise the carboxylate and weaken the acid.

optionRationale.1: Unsubstituted benzoic acid is weaker than the nitro substituted acid.
optionRationale.2: The methyl group is electron donating and lowers acidity.
optionRationale.4: The methoxy group is electron donating by resonance and lowers acidity.

questions.objective: Compare the acidity of substituted benzoic acids

questions.stem: Toluene is treated with chromyl chloride (CrO$_2$Cl$_2$) in carbon disulphide, and the chromium complex is then hydrolysed. The product is
questions.explanation: This is the Etard reaction. Chromyl chloride oxidises the methyl group of toluene to a chromium complex, which on hydrolysis gives benzaldehyde. The chromium complex protects the aldehyde group and prevents further oxidation to benzoic acid, which is why this method stops at benzaldehyde.

optionRationale.1: Benzoic acid is formed with strong oxidants such as alkaline KMnO$_4$.
optionRationale.2: Benzyl alcohol is a reduced product, not an oxidation product.
optionRationale.3: Acetophenone is made by Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene.

questions.stem: 0.60 g of a monocarboxylic acid (RCOOH) requires 10.0 mL of 1.00 M NaOH for complete neutralisation. What is the molar mass of the acid?
questions.explanation: A monocarboxylic acid reacts 1:1 with NaOH. Moles of NaOH = 1.00 x 0.0100 = 0.0100 mol, so moles of acid = 0.0100 mol. Molar mass = 0.60/0.0100 = 60 g mol$^{-1}$, which corresponds to ethanoic acid, CH$_3$COOH.

optionRationale.2: This assumes 2 mol of NaOH per mole of acid, which is true for a dicarboxylic acid.
optionRationale.3: This would result from 0.020 mol of acid, double the amount of NaOH.
optionRationale.4: This is a factor of ten too large, from a decimal slip in the volume.

questions.objective: Find molar mass of an acid by titration

questions.stem: A mixture of ethanal and propanal is treated with dilute NaOH. How many different aldol addition products (ignoring stereoisomers) can be formed?
questions.explanation: Both aldehydes have alpha-hydrogens and can act as enolate and as electrophile. This gives two self-aldol products (from ethanal-ethanal and from propanal-propanal) and two cross-aldol products (ethanal enolate with propanal, and propanal enolate with ethanal). The total is four.

optionRationale.1: Two counts only the self-addition products.
optionRationale.3: Three omits one of the two cross-aldol products.
optionRationale.4: Six overcounts; there are only four enolate-electrophile combinations.

questions.objective: Count products of a crossed aldol reaction

questions.stem: Benzaldehyde is heated with methanal in concentrated NaOH (crossed Cannizzaro reaction). The main products are
questions.explanation: In the crossed Cannizzaro reaction methanal is the more reactive aldehyde towards hydroxide addition and is oxidised, giving sodium formate. The hydride is transferred to benzaldehyde, which is reduced to benzyl alcohol. Neither aldehyde has an alpha-hydrogen.

optionRationale.1: This would need benzaldehyde to be oxidised and methanal to be reduced, which is the less common outcome.
optionRationale.2: This is the self-Cannizzaro outcome for benzaldehyde alone.
optionRationale.4: Free benzoic acid cannot form in a strongly basic solution, and benzaldehyde is not oxidised here.

questions.objective: Predict products of the crossed Cannizzaro reaction

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Ethanoic acid is a stronger acid than methanoic acid.
Reason (R): The methyl group in ethanoic acid has an electron releasing inductive effect, which destabilises the ethanoate ion.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: The methyl group donates electrons and destabilises the carboxylate ion, so the reason is true. This makes ethanoic acid (pK$_a$ 4.76) a weaker acid than methanoic acid (pK$_a$ 3.75), so the assertion is false.

optionRationale.1: The assertion is false, so (R) cannot explain it.
optionRationale.2: The assertion is false, so this option is wrong.
optionRationale.3: The reason is true: alkyl groups are electron releasing.

questions.objective: Compare acid strength using inductive effect

questions.stem: Match the reagent reacting with an aldehyde or ketone in List-I with the product type in List-II.
questions.explanation: The ammonia derivatives add to the carbonyl group and lose water. Hydroxylamine gives an oxime (A-III), hydrazine gives a hydrazone (B-II), 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine gives an orange 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone (C-IV) and semicarbazide gives a semicarbazone (D-I).

optionRationale.1: This code interchanges the matches of A and B; the correct pairs are A-III and B-II.
optionRationale.2: This code interchanges the matches of C and D; the correct pairs are C-IV and D-I.
optionRationale.3: This code interchanges the matches of A and C; the correct pairs are A-III and C-IV.

questions.objective: Match carbonyl derivatives with their reagents

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about carboxylic acids.
A. Carboxylic acids are stronger acids than phenols.
B. Benzoic acid is only sparingly soluble in cold water.
C. Esterification of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol is a reversible reaction.
D. Carboxylic acids are readily reduced by NaBH$_4$ to alcohols.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Carboxylate ions are stabilised by resonance over two equivalent oxygens, so carboxylic acids are stronger than phenols. Benzoic acid has a large hydrophobic ring and is sparingly soluble in cold water, and esterification is an equilibrium. NaBH$_4$ does not reduce carboxylic acids (LiAlH$_4$ does), so D is wrong.

optionRationale.2: D is wrong because NaBH$_4$ does not reduce acids, and C is also correct.
optionRationale.3: D is wrong, and A is correct.
optionRationale.4: It includes the wrong statement D and omits correct statements A and C.

questions.objective: Recall properties and reactions of carboxylic acids
